newsitem.title: ITALY: Roland Europe sales slip but 1997 in line.
newsitem.headline: Roland Europe sales slip but 1997 in line.

text.p: Roland Europe, the Italian-based maker of electronic musical instruments, saw sales drop 20 percent in the first four months of this year over the same 1996 period but sees 1997 profit in line with last year.

Chairman Carlo Lucarelli said turnover was down due to a general fall in consumer demand as well as usual seasonal effects, but profitability remained unchanged and the decline would be absorbed by the end of 1997 with full-year operating profit seen in line with 1996.
"We count on making up sales in the second half and on ending the year with operating profit equal to 13 percent of turnover, in line with 1996," he told reporters.

Lucarelli said the company was hoping for good sales from new products in the top range of digital keyboards and aimed for an aggressive commercial policy in order to reinforce the group's presence in France, Asia and the United States.
"At end-1997 turnover could be 5-10 percent lower but product profitability will rise," he said.

The company, controlled by the Roland Corp of Japan, posted 1996 net operating profit of 15.02 billion lire, up 32.8 percent. Net profit rose 77.9 percent to 12.72 billion lire on sales 1.5 percent down on 1995 at 107.8 billion lire.
The company said the decline in sales had been mostly due to a depreciation in the ecu used to invoice 95 percent of sales.
Quoted on the Milan bourse since June 1996, Roland shares at 1230 GMT were 0.57 percent off at 5,270 lire.
